evidence: We use the standard cross-validation method to split the datasets into 1/3 for training, 1/3 for testing, and 1/3 for validation, and report results as averages over 5 runs.
we evaluate our attacks and defenses extensively on four regression models (OLS, LASSO, ridge, and elastic net)
We use two main metrics for evaluating our algorithms: MSE for the effectiveness of the attacks and defenses, and running time for their cost.
We find that Chen has highly variable performance, having MSE increases of up to a factor of 63,087 over the no defense models
unresolved: n_baselines is compound: 1 baseline attack (BGD, adapted from Xiao et al.) for the attack evaluation, plus 4 baseline defenses (Huber, RANSAC, Chen, RONI) for the defense evaluation; reported as 5 total distinct comparison methods across both axes.

n_datasets counts only the three regression datasets used in the main evaluation (health care, loan, house pricing); the Contagio PDF classification dataset appears only in Appendix C as a reproduction of the Xiao et al. baseline attack in a classification setting, not part of the paper's own regression attack/defense evaluation.

n_eval_types set to 2 (MSE, running time) as the paper explicitly states these as 'two main metrics'; additional reported analyses (transferability ratio, dosage-change quantiles in the health case study) are derivatives of MSE rather than distinct metrics, so they were not counted separately.

reports_variability set to 'none' because MSE/running-time results in tables and figures appear to be single averaged values over the 5 runs with no std dev, CI, or error bars shown; variability is only discussed qualitatively in prose for the Chen defense's instability, not for the paper's own attack/defense results.

n_models could arguably be read as 5 if the classification models implicit in the Appendix C PDF baseline reproduction are counted, but that appendix reuses the classification setting only to validate BGD against Xiao et al., not as a distinct model evaluated across the main study.
